messages.content:
You are an expert synthetic chemist planning experiments to maximise reaction yield.
Each experiment chooses one option for every variable listed. You will see the results
of experiments already run. Choose the next batch to find the highest-yield conditions
in as few experiments as possible. Use chemical knowledge (ligand and base effects,
substrate reactivity, solvent effects) and the observed results. Balance exploiting
good regions with testing informative new combinations. Never repeat an experiment.
Return JSON only.

Pd-catalysed Buchwald-Hartwig amination of 4-chloroanisole with 4-methylaniline; choose the ligand, base and isoxazole additive.

Variables and options:
ligand:
L1: tBuBrettPhos [SMILES CC(C)C(C=C(C(C)C)C=C1C(C)C)=C1C2=C(P(C(C)(C)C)C(C)(C)C)C(OC)=CC=C2OC]
L2: tBuXPhos [SMILES CC(C)C(C=C(C(C)C)C=C1C(C)C)=C1C2=C(P(C(C)(C)C)C(C)(C)C)C=CC=C2]
L3: XPhos [SMILES CC(C)C(C=C(C(C)C)C=C1C(C)C)=C1C2=C(P(C3CCCCC3)C4CCCCC4)C=CC=C2]
L4: AdBrettPhos [SMILES CC(C)C(C=C(C(C)C)C=C1C(C)C)=C1C2=C(P([C@@]3(C[C@@H]4C5)C[C@H](C4)C[C@H]5C3)[C@]6(C7)C[C@@H](C[C@@H]7C8)C[C@@H]8C6)C(OC)=CC=C2OC]

B1: BTMG [SMILES CC(C)(C)/N=C(N(C)C)/N(C)C]

B3: MTBD [SMILES CN1CCCN2C1=NCCC2]

picks.reason: This tests whether the best observed additive transfers to the more electron-rich BrettPhos catalyst.
A compact dimethylisoxazole probes whether a small, weakly coordinating additive benefits this catalyst and base.
This tests a minimally substituted isoxazole under the promising BTMG base.
The dibenzylamino substituent provides a strongly donating additive variant to test for beneficial catalyst modulation.
This pairs BrettPhos and the strong phosphazene base with a simple phenyl-substituted isoxazole.
Changing the phenylisoxazole substitution pattern tests whether additive structure affects the phosphazene-base conditions.
The ester-substituted isoxazole tests a more electron-poor additive with BrettPhos and P2Et.
This tests an electron-rich methoxyisoxazole ester in a strong-base catalyst system.
The fused benzisoxazole probes a distinct additive scaffold with the BrettPhos catalyst.
The compact isoxazole ester tests an electron-withdrawing additive under MTBD conditions.
This checks whether the best observed additive pairs effectively with the bulky AdBrettPhos ligand.
The pyrrolyl-substituted isoxazole tests a larger, potentially donating additive with BTMG.
This tests a methyl- and phenyl-substituted isoxazole with the bulky ligand and promising BTMG base.
The ester-bearing isoxazole tests a distinct substitution pattern with AdBrettPhos and P2Et.
This tests an isoxazole-4-carboxylate additive under strong-base conditions.
This probes an isoxazole-3-carboxylate with AdBrettPhos and the less-explored MTBD base.
This tests a simple alkyl-substituted additive with tBuXPhos under the base used in the best observed run.
The amino-substituted additive tests a strongly donating variant with tBuXPhos and P2Et.
This tests a simple isoxazole additive while varying both ligand and base from the previous tBuXPhos result.
This tests whether a phenylisoxazole additive improves the XPhos–BTMG combination beyond the previously weak result.
